findings.text: The INC-2026-016 postmortem names two root causes: CHG-3340 (ledger, 2026-03-13 18:40 UTC), which reduced DB connection pool max_connections from 240 to 60, and CHG-3357 (fraud-scoring, 2026-03-14 08:55 UTC), the v1.5.8 deploy with a new scoring model and feature pipeline.
The change log confirms CHG-3340 (ledger, config, Payments Core, risk high) and CHG-3357 (fraud-scoring, deploy v1.5.8, Risk team, risk high), with the same timestamps.
During INC-2026-016, ledger was degraded from 2026-03-14 09:12 UTC to 12:52 UTC: payment authorisations queued and the ledger connection pool ran out while fraud scoring latency rose to 2.4 s.
INC-2026-016 impact: 220 minutes, 34% of payments delayed in the window. Affected services: ledger, fraud-scoring, payments-api, payout-service, reconciliation, notifications.

The INC-2026-018 postmortem gives the root cause as CHG-3499 (bank-connector, 2026-03-20 20:44 UTC), which enabled flag batch_settlement_v2 for 100% of traffic. The change log confirms it (flag, v1.5.3, Money Movement, risk medium).

During INC-2026-018, bank-connector was degraded from 2026-03-20 22:13 UTC to 2026-03-21 00:23 UTC, with settlement batches stuck in PENDING. Impact: 130 minutes, 27% of payments delayed. Affected services: bank-connector, card-processor, payout-service, reconciliation.
The INC-2026-014 postmortem gives the root cause as CHG-3139 (payments-api, 2026-03-03 05:12 UTC), Run migration M1938: add index on transactions(created_at). The change log confirms it.

INC-2026-014: a table lock blocked writes to the transactions table from 10:50 to 11:45 UTC on 2026-03-03. Impact: 55 minutes, 3% of payments delayed. Affected services: payments-api, api-gateway, merchant-portal.

The public status pages give earlier resolution times than the postmortems: INC-2026-016 at 2026-03-14 11:12 UTC (postmortem 12:52 UTC) and INC-2026-018 at 2026-03-20 22:43 UTC (postmortem 2026-03-21 00:23 UTC). The postmortem times are preferred.
The incident reports written during INC-2026-016 and INC-2026-018 list fewer affected services than the postmortems that superseded them.
